quotes.text: Cash App Pay refunds are never processed as reversals.
Cash App Pay payments can only be disputed once.
Dispute fees are non-refundable regardless of the outcome.

old_evidence.text: US customers (excluding accounts in US territories) and US-based travelers1.
Customers have 120 calendar days to file a dispute from the date of the original charge, or in situations where they didn’t receive goods, 120 calendar days from the expected receipt date.
Set the `cashapp_payments` capability to `active` on your platform account, and for any connected accounts you want to enable for Cash App Pay.
Cash App Pay supports partial or full refunds for up to 90 days after the original purchase, and processes them asynchronously.

findings: November overview adds explicit US merchant/customer and USD domestic eligibility, 0.50 USD transaction minimum, B2C-only account model, post-activation eligibility review and a concrete prohibited/restricted MCC table (new raw lines 16-104). May overview had US/USD and broad prohibited categories, and explicitly included US-based travelers able to access Cash App (old raw lines 21-77, 111-118). A customer-country table is not proof that the earlier traveler exception has ended; preserve it as dated and flag uncertainty.

November labels merchant payment-method access as 'Instant provisional access' and says the account may be reviewed for eligibility after activation (new raw lines 12, 18-23). Separately, it labels an individual payment's confirmation timing immediate and settlement up to T+2 business days (new raw lines 13-14). Method access is not a phase of that payment and does not become permanent when its funds settle. The capture also adds a capability matrix: recurring, manual and partial capture, full/partial refunds, full but not partial disputes, and no extended/incremental/decremental/reauthorization, multicapture or overcapture (new raw lines 110-135). Payment confirmation is distinct from settlement.

Both captures retain 90-day asynchronous refund submission and succeeded/failed webhook/object outcome tracking (old raw lines 120-124; new raw lines 126-150). November adds up-to-10-business-day processing, non-cancelability, no reversal treatment, and direct return to the original Cash App balance or linked source (new raw lines 129-150). Submitted refund is not a completed refund; failure restores the Stripe balance and requires another customer refund route.

Both captures retain 13-day evidence and a final decision within 58 days, with on-session Cash App versus saved off-session merchant consumer-fraud liability and business-of-record cloning limit (old raw lines 126-155, 165-197; new raw lines 152-200). November adds a once-only, full-dispute-only limit, explicit nonrefundable dispute fee even on a merchant win, reason/evidence_due_by fields, Dashboard/API evidence path and Files API IDs (new raw lines 132-190). The old page also gave an expected-receipt-date trigger for nondelivery disputes; the new page says 120 days from purchase (old raw line 132; new raw line 154). Retain the old trigger as dated and flag the unresolved scope conflict rather than silently dropping it.

November adds a product/API matrix, a 10-minute app authentication step, and eligibility framing (new raw lines 202-245). The separate May integration guide describes a 60-minute authentication session and QR refreshes, but also specifically says a requires_action PaymentIntent must complete within 10 minutes after redirect or detaches the PaymentMethod and returns to requires_payment_method (raw/stripe-cash-app-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:1130-1144, 1226-1234). The clocks have different triggers and should be stated with scope; do not replace the dated 60-minute session claim with a universal 10-minute session.

The May overview's Connect cashapp_payments active-capability prerequisite is omitted from November, although November lists Connect support and account eligibility (old raw lines 165-171; new raw lines 18-23, 211-224). Keep the active-capability detail dated pending a current Connect variant; the same business-of-record descriptor map and no-cloning boundary persist (old raw lines 173-197; new raw lines 198-200, 247-273). New account presentation of prohibited versus restricted MCCs must not erase the May broader platform/alcohol/gift-card restrictions without category/role reconciliation (old raw lines 111-118; new raw lines 25-89).

The mapped source reflects the May overview's core funding, refund, fraud-liability and Connect identity constraints but lacks November settlement, minimum, capability exclusions, refund finality, once-only/full dispute and fee details (source lines 13-42). Its mobile 'auto-authenticated' phrase at line 19 needs an outcome caveat: November says the customer has 10 minutes to authenticate, and returning to checkout is not by itself proof of payment (new raw lines 231-245). Context at wiki/concepts/stripe-wallets.md:133-159 repeats the May 60-minute integration window, which is scoped by the separate guide above.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/cash-app-pay, the November capture describes a US/USD domestic B2C wallet funded by full Cash App balance or a linked debit card, subject to category limits and a 0.50 USD transaction floor. Its 'Instant provisional access' label concerns merchant access to Cash App Pay, with possible account eligibility review after activation; separately, an individual payment has immediate confirmation timing and up-to-T+2 settlement timing. Method access is not a payment state or made permanent by settlement. Recurring and manual/partial capture are supported, while several authorization and capture variants are not. Refunds have a 90-day submission window, asynchronous succeeded/failed outcomes, and a 10-business-day processing bound; disputes are full-only and once-only with 13-day evidence, 58-day decision and nonrefundable fees. On-session customer-fraud liability rests with Cash App, saved off-session liability with the business of record; Connect cloning across different such businesses is barred. Old raw lines 12-77, 106-197 support much of the core but omit several new limits; new raw lines 9-245 add them. source-stripe-cash-app-pay.md captures older funding/liability but needs these distinct access, payment and eligibility states. Redirect, authentication, refund submission and dispute evidence are not final payment/refund/dispute outcomes.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/cash-app-pay, the new eligibility/MCC, 0.50 USD minimum, capability exclusions, refund non-cancel/no-reversal/10-day processing, full-once-only dispute and fee-finality fields are substantive additions (old raw lines 21-77, 111-155; new raw lines 10-190). The new merchant-access label and post-activation account review must be distinguished from immediate individual-payment confirmation and T+2 settlement. Table normalization and moved branding/descriptor/Connect sections are presentation. source-stripe-cash-app-pay.md must preserve May provenance and warn reciprocally that May allowed an expected-receipt start for nondelivery disputes and US-based travelers, while November says purchase-date and domestic-US only; neither omission alone proves policy cancellation. The November 10-minute app step should be scoped against the separate May integration guide's 60-minute session and 10-minute post-redirect requires_action deadline. Retain old Connect capability detail as dated, distinguish business of record from platform/connected account, and never infer success from QR scan, redirect, payment confirmation, refund request or evidence submission; verify object/webhook outcome and settlement separately.
